name: Progressive Symmetric Erythrokeratodermia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Progressive Symmetric Erythrokeratodermia

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, symmetrical erythematous and hyperkeratotic plaques predominantly on the extremities and trunk
Progressive development of lesions with gradual enlargement and thickening over months to years
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and mild perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of mutations in connexin genes GJB3 or GJB4

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetrical erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques with progressive course and supportive histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical presentation and histology are primary.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and mild perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent erythema with less hyperkeratosis
More extensive hyperkeratosis with spiky or verrucous plaques

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with ulceration
Signs of secondary bacterial infection with systemic symptoms
Development of joint contractures or functional impairment
references: Hennies HC, et al. Mutations in GJB3 cause erythrokeratodermia variabilis. Nat Genet. 2004.
